featured_reviews.review_text:
There is a woman named Nidhi who runs NM One Roof in Bhayandar West. Unfortunately, my experience with her has been extremely disappointing.
I had enrolled my 4-year-old twins in the football classes there. After just three sessions, she abruptly demanded a ₹400 fine for the unpaid sessions and spoke to me in a very rude and disrespectful manner.
Earlier that day, I had called her to inform that one of my children had a fever and that we would not be able to attend the class. I also told her that I would pay the fees in the next session and requested if she could allow an extra session later due to the medical reason. Since the twins are always together, it is quite obvious that the other child might also get affected, and missing the class would mean a loss for us. Despite explaining this situation politely, she refused to consider it.
Later, as my child was feeling slightly better after taking medicine and both my kids really wanted to attend football, I decided to bring them for the class.
However, when I reached her office, she started speaking very harshly about the payment not being made earlier. What shocked me even more was that she started questioning my motherhood and said things like, “You are not the only person in the world handling two kids. It’s your problem, not mine. You have to manage your children.”
I found this extremely disrespectful and completely unacceptable. No one has the right to comment on someone’s parenting like that.
The situation became so uncomfortable that I told her I would discontinue the classes and that I would still pay the fees for the three sessions.
Even after I left her office, she came outside and sarcastically asked, “If your child has a fever, how are you out of the house?”
This behavior was shocking and completely unprofessional. She clearly lacks the basic sense of how to speak with parents or clients. It was a very unpleasant and disturbing experience.

featured_reviews.review_text: I had a very disappointing and shocking experience with Adv. Nidhi Mishra at NM One Roof. If a professional cannot handle simple queries from parents with respect, it creates a serious doubt about their ability to nurture and manage children. I would advise parents to think twice before enrolling their kids in this academy.

featured_reviews.name: Sandesh Padyar
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a well-developed infrastructure project by the VVMC. Inaugurated in 2009, the pool has been operational regularly for the last 17 years (except during the COVID-19 pandemic), which is highly commendable. If you want to pursue swimming as a hobby at an affordable rate of just 500 INR per month, this is a great choice.
​Pros:
​Olympic Size: Because it is built to Olympic standards, it easily handles a crowd of 70 to 80 members per batch without feeling overly congested.
​Water Upkeep: Water cleanliness issues arise occasionally, but the management is generally quick to address and resolve them.
​Cons & Areas for Improvement:
​Staff Management: Except for 2 or 3 efficient lifeguards, the rest of the staff is quite passive. They also tend to rush members out, closing the batch 10 minutes prior to the official end time.
​Changing Room Maintenance: The facility lacks basic amenities. The locker system has been discontinued, there are no racks to store bags, and there aren't enough benches to sit on while changing.
​Plumbing & Safety: The shower taps and fittings are in poor condition. Additionally, there are no anti-skid mats installed in the changing or shower areas, making them slippery and unsafe.
​Verdict: An excellent budget-friendly Olympic-sized facility for local residents, provided you can overlook the average upkeep of the changing rooms.
